 Keldon Johnson tallied 18 points (6-of-11 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), four rebounds, four assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Warriors.
 Johnson’s scoring average has dropped considerably after he averaged 13.2 points per game and won NBA Sixth Man of the Year last season. The Spurs forward entered Friday averaging 8.0 points per game on 44.6 percent shooting. Given those numbers, Johnson needed a night like Friday, even if he scored nine of his points in the fourth quarter of a game the Spurs won by 38. Johnson is rostered in eight percent of Yahoo leagues, a fair percentage given the lackluster production.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 De’Aaron Fox (hip) is questionable to play against the Warriors on Friday. 
 Fox could end up missing a game for the first time this season. If that happens, Dylan Harper and Stephon Castle would likely see a bump in usage. Devin Vassell has been sidelined but is questionable as well. If he returns and Fox is out, Julian Champagnie will continue to start. If both are out, Keldon Johnson or Carter Bryant could enter the starting lineup.

 Devin Vassell (groin) is out for Monday’s matchup with the Suns. 
 Vassell will miss his first game of the season, which should free up more playing time for Julian Champagnie and Keldon Johnson. Both are work a look for fantasy managers in need of streaming assistance.

 Keldon Johnson (mouth) is available to play on Friday against the Rockets. 
 Keldon Johnson suffered a laceration in his mouth against the Thunder. He will be available and likely play as normal. He can be used as a streamer for points and rebounds.

 Keldon Johnson (mouth) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Rockets. 
 Johnson suffered a laceration to his mouth during Tuesday’s loss to the Thunder, but he still played 20 minutes off the bench. He’ll likely carry a similar workload if he’s available on Friday. If Johnson can’t play, Harrison Barnes and Carter Bryant stand to gain the most in playing time. 
 Keldon Johnson 
 SAS 
 Forward-Guard 
 #3 
 Keldon Johnson amassed 15 points (4-of-10 FGs, 7-of-9 FTs), four rebounds, four assists and two steals in Monday’s exhibition against the Jazz. 
 Johnson, the reigning NBA Sixth Man of the Year, was inserted into the Spurs’ starting lineup on Monday. Obviously, he won’t be asked to fill that role very often once the regular season begins. Another issue for Johnson’s fantasy outlook is the emergence of Dylan Harper, even though they don’t play the same position, and the addition of Tobias Harris. The deeper rotation means someone will lose playing time, and that could be Johnson. 
 Dylan Harper 
 SAS 
 Guard 
 #2 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that Dylan Harper (adductor) will be a game-time decision for Friday’s Game 3 against the Thunder. 
 Harper had a monster Game 1 but was forced out of Game 2 after only 25 minutes with what was believed to be a right leg injury. An MRI revealed a right adductor injury, and there’s a chance Harper is forced to sit out Game 3. De’Aaron Fox (ankle) is also questionable, and San Antonio’s backcourt could be shorthanded in a pivotal home showdown. Keldon Johnson and Jordan McLaughlin could be in line for expanded roles, with Stephon Castle and Devin Vassell doing some heavy lifting.
 Dylan Harper 
 SAS 
 Guard 
 #2 
 Dylan Harper (adductor) is questionable for Friday’s Game 3 against the Thunder. 
 Harper, who started the first two games of the Western Conference Finals for the injured De’Aaron Fox (ankle), exited Game 2 after playing 25 minutes due to a sore right adductor. How impactful his absence would be in Game 3 depends on Fox; if the veteran point guard can return, the Spurs will be able to compensate for Harper’s absence. However, if both sit, Keldon Johnson could move into the starting lineup, with Jordan McLaughlin’s playing time increasing. 
 Keldon Johnson 
 SAS 
 Forward-Guard 
 #3 
 Keldon Johnson accounted for 21 points (8-of-11 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), two rebounds, two steals, one block and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s Game 5 win over the Timberwolves. 
 Having averaged 8.8 points per game in the first four games of the series, Johnson stepped up in a big way in Game 5. Aggressive from the start, the Spurs forward finished with a playoff career-high 21 points. Johnson wasn’t the only Spurs reserve to step up on Tuesday, as rookie Dylan Harper added a double-double with 12 points (5-of-10 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 10 rebounds, two assists, one steal and one blocked shot. A win in Game 6 on Friday would send the Spurs to the conference finals for the first time since 2017. 
 De'Aaron Fox 
 SAS 
 Guard 
 #4 
 De’Aaron Fox recorded 28 points (11-of-17 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, seven assists, one steal, two blocks and four three-pointers in Sunday’s Game 4 win over the Trail Blazers. 
 The Spurs outscored Portland by a 73-35 margin in the second half, and Fox played a major part in that. He scored 18 of his 28 points in the second half and also had a few key assists to Keldon Johnson (9/1/1/1 with one three-pointer) in the fourth quarter. Fox put up a complete stat line in Game 4, and he’ll look to do the same in Game 5 on Tuesday. The Spurs hold a 3-1 series lead, so Sunday may have been their last visit to Portland this season. 
 Keldon Johnson 
 SAS 
 Forward-Guard 
 #3 
 Keldon Johnson was named the 2025-26 NBA Sixth Man of the Year on Wednesday. 
 Two days after his teammate, Victor Wembanyama, won Defensive Player of the Year, Johnson now brings home the Sixth Man award. The honor highlights the seventh-year forward’s contributions and impact off the bench, averaging 13.2 points and 5.4 rebounds in all 82 regular-season games. He joins Manu Ginobili as the only Spurs players to win the award.

 Isaiah Hartenstein notched 21 points (9-of-10 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), 16 rebounds, six assists and one steal in Friday’s loss to the Clippers.
 After scoring no more than seven points in any of Oklahoma City’s first five games in November, Hartenstein has scored at least 20 in two straight games. He was outstanding against the Clippers, shooting 90 percent from the field and providing excellent value in points, rebounds and assists. Providing top-100 fantasy value, Hartenstein is rostered in 84 percent of Yahoo leagues. Given Oklahoma City’s frontcourt injuries, those rostering Hartenstein would be better served holding on to him than entertaining a trade after the last two games.

 Jared McCain tallied 23 points (8-of-17 FGs), four rebounds, two assists and seven three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Clippers.
 McCain has scored in double figures in four straight games, with Friday’s being the best of the bunch. The Thunder guard shot 7-of-11 from deep against the Clippers, recording season highs in points and three-pointers. McCain will mainly be a “points and triples” option in fantasy leagues, but Oklahoma City’s injuries open the door for him to provide consistent value.

 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander finished Friday’s loss to the Clippers with 40 points (15-of-26 FGs, 8-of-11 FTs), four rebounds, five assists, one steal and two three-pointers.
 Gilgeous-Alexander finished with his third 40-point game of the season, but he wishes he’d scored 42 instead of 40. The two-time MVP’s shot as time expired missed the mark, resulting in a 113-112 Clippers victory. After shooting a combined 17-of-42 in two losses to the Trail Blazers, Gilgeous-Alexander was much more efficient on Friday, shooting well over 50 percent from the field. He could be in for another big night to end the week, as the Thunder visit the Kings on Sunday. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Keaton Wagler produced 14 points (4-of-7 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), two rebounds, one assist and two three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Thunder.
 After reaching double figures in each of his first five games, Wagler totaled 13 points on 4-of-13 shooting in the Clippers’ first two games of November. The rookie has gotten back on track, having scored at least 11 points in four straight games. Wagler remains a deep-league option in redraft formats, while dynasty league managers should be excited for the rookie guard’s future.

 Derrick Jones Jr. accounted for 14 points (5-of-10 FGs), five rebounds, one steal, four blocks and four three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Thunder.
 Thanks mainly to the three-pointers and defensive stats, Jones has been close to a top-100 player in nine-cat formats. Against the Thunder, he shot 4-of-7 from beyond the arc and recorded five “stocks” in 29 minutes. This was Jones’ fourth game this season with at least two three-pointers, one steal and one block. Managers needing help in those categories should consider adding Jones ahead of Sunday’s game against the Hornets.

 Brook Lopez accumulated 26 points (11-of-21 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Thunder.
 After coming off the bench in the Clippers’ first six games, Lopez is approaching the point where he needs to be rostered in 12-team leagues. He’s scored at least 20 points in three of the last four games, with Friday’s total being a season high. Add in the rebounds and three-pointers, and this was a good night for those rostering the veteran center. Isaiah Jackson (5/3/3 with one block), who began the season as the starter, should be rostered only in very deep leagues.

 Darius Garland finished Friday’s win over the Thunder with 24 points (8-of-17 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), four rebounds, seven assists, one block and three three-pointers.
 After being outscored 40-25 in the third quarter, Garland and the Clippers did what needed to be done down the stretch to win the 113-112 thriller. The Clippers’ starting point guard had the game’s biggest shot: a layup through contact and an ensuing free throw with 50.4 seconds left to take the lead for good. Even with the occasional struggles with turnovers, Garland is providing top-100 fantasy value through 11 games. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Domantas Sabonis put up 21 points (9-of-16 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 12 rebounds, five assists, and a three in the loss on Friday to the Blazers. 
 After a really bad game against the Magic, Sabonis bounced back and went back to his usual self against the Blazers. He looked healthier in this game, which is a good sign. The efficiency has still been good, but it is starting to come down from his super-hot start. He still puts up good counting stats which is why you have Sabonis in the first place. Overall, its been a good season so far.
